html:
K'ómoks First Nation is a community on the east coast of Vancouver Island, around the Comox Valley in British Columbia. Its people descend from the Coast Salish Pentlatch and Comox peoples and from Kwakwaka'wakw groups who moved south into the area in the 1800s, so their heritage joins two language families.

The waters of the valley gave herring, salmon and shellfish. Thousands of wooden stakes from old fish traps, some over a thousand years old, still show at low tide in the Comox estuary. Disease cut their numbers in the 1800s, and their reserve today is small. Their neighbours include the Tla'amin, Klahoose and Kwakwaka'wakw.
